blockingIssues.description: fluxos-cli/src/runtime/toolRuntime.ts:26 hard-codes a runtime import of ../../../flux-mcp/dist/index.js, so the generic runner only works when the sibling MCP package has already been built in that repo-relative location instead of preserving a standalone/shared-runtime boundary.

fluxos-cli/test/tool-runner.test.ts:63 does not actually cover a tool with an existing first-class CLI wrapper, so the assigned coverage requirement for tools with and without first-class surfaces remains unmet.

fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:599 ignores structuredContent.ok === false unless isError is also set, so real MCP tools such as flux_auth_diagnose can be normalized as ok/exit 0 even when they intentionally return a negative result envelope.

fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:443 uses auth-failure phrase matching that is too narrow, so real auth-required MCP failures such as enterprise spec decryption prerequisites fall through to Flux exit code 6 instead of the required auth exit code 3.

fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:597 forwards MCP nextActions unchanged, but machine-followed resource reads still hit the MCP in-memory store through flux_resource_read rather than the persisted CLI resource store, so suggested follow-up actions break across fresh CLI invocations.
